responses:
{
  "summary": "The draft is still a blank slate — no title, description, or premise — so any quality set I invent now would be guesswork that we'd have to tear out later. Before I define what the story measures each turn (progress, danger, trust, resources), I need a few anchors about what kind of story this is and what its central dramatic question is.",
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "premise",
      "text": "What's the premise and genre of this story?",
      "why": "Qualities have to be readable from the prose the chat actually produces — a survival horror, a political intrigue, and a romance all need different measurements.",
      "options": [
        "Survival / horror",
        "Political intrigue or court drama",
        "Romance / relationship-driven",
        "Heist or quest adventure",
        "Mystery / investigation",
        "Something else (describe it)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "central_question",
      "text": "What is the central dramatic question the player is pushing toward?",
      "why": "The answer becomes the spine of the progress quality and the anchor checkpoints — without it, gates have nothing meaningful to test.",
      "options": [
        "Do they escape / survive the threat?",
        "Do they win the prize, the throne, or the objective?",
        "Do they earn the trust or love of a key character?",
        "Do they uncover the truth behind the mystery?",
        "Something else (describe it)"
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "tracked_pressures",
      "text": "Which ongoing pressures should the story track turn to turn?",
      "why": "These become extractor qualities with rubrics; each one needs to be visibly stated or shown in the prose to be usable.",
      "options": [
        "Danger level rising toward a breaking point",
        "Trust or standing with one key ally (latching decision points)",
        "A dwindling resource (time, coin, supplies, health)",
        "Suspicion / exposure risk from a watching antagonist",
        "Momentum toward the goal (monotonic progress)",
        "Let me pick a mix (describe)"
      ]
    }
  ]
}

responses: {"summary":"The install already carries the story's lorebook (Vault Job Lore) and no Vex card or crew group exists yet. I'll create the Vex card (the crew's lockpick, present in the opening beat so she gets a first message), add three lorebook entries to Vault Job Lore for the bank, the vault door and the vault key the start checkpoint turns on, and create the group 'The Vault Job' with Vex as its only member.","ops":[{"kind":"createCharacterCard","name":"Vex","description":"Vex is a wiry, sharp-eyed lockpick in her late twenties, the best in the city at talking a lock out of its secrets. She wears a battered leather jacket over a tool roll, keeps her dark hair shoved under a flat cap, and treats every job like a puzzle that owes her an answer. She talks fast, jokes when she's nervous, and never touches a lock she hasn't already studied from three angles.","role":"The crew's lockpick — the one who reads locks and opens what the crew can't.","personality":"Restless, cocky, precise. Vex fidgets with picks while she thinks, needles anyone who stands still too long, and goes quiet and dead-calm the moment a real mechanism is in front of her. She hates being rushed and hates being wrong more.","scenario":"Vex is casing the city bank from the street outside, working out how the crew gets in and where the vault key is kept.","first_mes":"*Vex is leaning against the lamppost across from the bank, one boot heel tapping, a folded newspaper under her arm that she hasn't read a word of. Her eyes keep drifting back to the side door where the guards trade off shifts.*\n\n\"Four minutes late on the changeover,\" *she says without looking at you.* \"Every night. That's four minutes of nobody watching a very interesting corridor.\" *She finally turns, grinning, and flicks a pick between her fingers.* \"So. Tell me you've got something better than 'we walk in and hope,' because I've read this building's locks from the street and they're not the problem. The vault is. And the vault wants a key we don't have. Yet.\"","tags":["thief","lockpick","heist","crew"]},{"kind":"upsertLorebookEntry","lorebook":"Vault Job Lore","comment":"The City Bank","keys":["city bank","the bank","bank"],"content":"The City Bank is the oldest building on Market Row: a stone front, a brass-and-glass lobby, a teller floor, and a back corridor the public never sees. Guards work in pairs and change over on a fixed nightly rotation — the changeover leaves the side corridor unwatched for about four minutes. The manager's office sits off that corridor, and the manager is the only person who carries a key to the lower level."},{"kind":"upsertLorebookEntry","lorebook":"Vault Job Lore","comment":"The Vault Door","keys":["vault","vault door","the vault"],"content":"The vault sits in the bank's lower level behind a steel door with a twin-tumbler lock and a keyway that has never been picked — not by Vex, not by anyone she's heard of. The door is the crew's real obstacle: it can be worked on, but it cannot be talked open. It needs the vault key, turned by someone who knows the mechanism's order of operations."},{"kind":"upsertLorebookEntry","lorebook":"Vault Job Lore","comment":"The Vault Key","keys":["vault key","the key"],"content":"The vault key is a long, heavy brass thing on a leather fob, kept on the bank manager's person at all times and never left in the building overnight. Without it the vault door stays shut. Getting the key — by theft, trade, trickery or leverage — is what the crew's casing job is really for."},{"kind":"createGroup","name":"The Vault Job","members":["Vex"]}]}
